topic: Stable-orbit counting complexity for cyclic linear non-Gaussian mechanisms. For square fully observed cyclic LiNG SEMs identified up to normalized ICA row assignments, let N_stab(W) count every admissible normalized row assignment whose induced coefficient matrix is Schur stable. Prove that for every simple n-vertex graph G an explicit rational 3n-variable construction W_G, with epsilon_n=1/[2^40(n+1)^4], has its complete stable assignment orbit in bijection with the independent sets of G; derive #P-completeness under polynomial-time Turing reductions and no FPRAS unless RP=NP on the stated bounded-degree images, contrasted with the permanent FPRAS for unfiltered assignments. Prove exact SCC factorization and an output-sensitive local enumeration algorithm. Add pointwise orbit-honest count inference by inverting a symmetrized FOBI confidence region, without uniform graph-support claims. Consumer: the matching-frequency sampler and adaptive intervention choice of Sharifian, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash must condition on stability when equilibrium stability is imposed. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Exact elimination gives an analytic critical-root coordinate with perturbation bounded by 4gn^2; explicit radial margins separate independent from non-independent switch sets, while resolvent contours exclude root-third-coordinate swaps and root-only cycles. Complete rational enumeration at the committed epsilon rule matched independent-set counts for K2, P5, C5, K1,4, and K5, with stable counts 3, 13, 11, 17, and 6 and no extra or missing assignment. Counting/AP conventions, polynomial bit length, error-law closure, SCC factorization, and the consumer mapping survived destructive checks. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently verify the graph-uniform analytic determinant homotopy, especially multiplicity preservation and absence of poles after the Schur complement and local inverse map. EARLY KILL TEST: Audit the exact pencil, inverse-coordinate equations, 4gn^2 bound, and negative-mode homotopy, then rerun all five exact complete-orbit checks; any sign error, hidden pole, lost polynomial-bit margin, or unintended stable permutation kills the realization. open_problems.open_problem: Determine the exact and randomized-approximation complexity of counting Schur-stable normalized ICA row assignments in fully observed cyclic LiNG SEMs, including bounded-degree assignment images.

source_refs.claim: Distribution-equivalent cyclic LiNG graphs correspond to perfect matchings; reward estimation samples those matchings without a stability filter.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Prior CausalSmith work and the published cyclic-LiNG literature establish normalized row-assignment and perfect-matching representations but treat stability only as a candidate-level filter or omit it. Stability is a global spectral predicate, so ordinary matching gadgets do not control normalization, feedback cancellation, invertibility, or graph-uniform eigenvalue margins. The proposed independent-set construction remains unverified at its decisive step: multiplicity preservation and absence of poles through the determinant homotopy and Schur-complement inverse map. Rejection sampling from the permanent FPRAS can also be exponentially inefficient when the stable suborbit is sparse.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit polynomial-bit rational reduction giving a bijection between independent sets and all Schur-stable assignments, proving #P-completeness under polynomial-time Turing reductions and no FPRAS on a stated bounded-degree image class unless RP=NP, alongside the permanent-FPRAS result for the unfiltered orbit.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from observational ambiguity to a matching orbit and then to the computational burden of querying that orbit, with equilibrium stability as the missing filter.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Cyclic LiNG observations identify a permutation-equivalence class -> the class is represented by perfect matchings -> adaptive decisions require orbit frequencies -> equilibrium stability turns the frequency oracle into stable-orbit counting

method_exemplars.technique: Define the complete causal orbit through admissible normalized row permutations and then apply spectral stability screening, using cycle-reversal arguments to track feedback products.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the precise causal orbit and stability predicate whose joint counting complexity must be classified.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer approximation hardness from bounded-degree hard-core configurations using phase-separated gadget behavior.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Independent sets are the intended stable-assignment witnesses, and this result supplies the bounded-degree no-FPRAS source problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Use annealed Markov-chain sampling of perfect and near-perfect matchings, self-reduction, and multiplicative concentration to estimate the permanent.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives the exact approximation benchmark for the unfiltered assignment orbit and exposes what the stability-conditioned problem loses.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish whether the Schur-stable ICA assignment orbit factors exactly over identifiable strongly connected components and consequently admits duplicate-free output-sensitive local enumeration.

source_refs.author: Ehsan Sharifian, Saber Salehkaleybar, Negar Kiyavash

open_problems.why_unsolved: Published SCC invariance and block-triangular spectral arguments do not by themselves prove that admissible normalized row assignments form a Cartesian product across components: matching constraints, normalization, and assignment-induced support changes could couple blocks. Prior enumeration work additionally materializes an exponential subset-state space and explicitly falls short of polynomial delay. The first new proof step must establish a canonical, assignment-invariant component decomposition and a complete future-extension congruence before a stability test can be localized.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem specifying conditions under which N_stab(W)=product_C N_stab(W_C), together with a complete exact-once local enumerator having polynomial preprocessing and delay polynomial in the input and each emitted stable assignment.

writing_exemplar.why: Its narrative moves from unnecessary global recovery to exact local alternatives and then isolates the extra constraint created by stability.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Global cyclic recovery can be excessive -> local ICA/ISA recovers identifiable local alternatives -> stability still appears global -> SCC factorization would reduce stable-orbit recovery to local enumeration

method_exemplars.technique: Combine cycle-reversion analysis proving SCC preservation with the bipartite perfect-matching representation of admissible assignments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: SCC preservation is the first structural lemma required before the assignment orbit can decompose.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt recursive alternating-cycle generation of all bipartite perfect matchings with bounded work per output.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A stable local enumerator must refine this unfiltered enumeration machinery without traversing exponentially many rejected matchings.

open_problems.why_unsolved: FOBI asymptotics and the prior CausalSmith confidence frontier are locally indexed by a labelled or fixed normalized ICA representation. The causal target is instead invariant to the complete permutation-and-scaling orbit and then applies discrete admissibility and spectral tests. Its value jumps when a normalization diagonal vanishes or an eigenvalue crosses the unit circle, invalidating a direct delta method and precluding uniform graph-support recovery without separation assumptions. The missing construction is an equivariant finite-group confidence region followed by exact inversion through this discontinuous count functional.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A random set C_n={N_stab(W): W belongs to a symmetrized FOBI region} with pointwise asymptotic coverage at least 1-alpha and consistency under explicit normalization and radial margins, plus a local sequence demonstrating failure of uniform honesty at assignment or unit-circle boundaries.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its transition from ICA indeterminacy to asymptotic accuracy, but propagate uncertainty to the full causal orbit rather than selecting an arbitrary labelling.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: ICA identifies sources modulo scaling and permutation -> FOBI estimates an unmixing functional with a joint limit law -> uncertainty must respect the symmetry orbit -> invert the orbit region for pointwise coverage of the stable count

method_exemplars.technique: Linearize the FOBI estimating equations and derive the joint asymptotic covariance of the vectorized unmixing estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: That Gaussian matrix limit is the required input to a confidence region whose full symmetry orbit can be inverted.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct coverage-valid regions before projecting the entire region through a set-valued or nonsmooth target map.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Region-first inversion is structurally suited to the discontinuous stable-assignment count.

method_exemplars.technique: Use contiguous local perturbations at discontinuity points to disprove locally uniform nontrivial confidence guarantees.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Zero-normalization and unit-circle boundaries are precisely discontinuities of the stable-orbit count.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing intervention scores and prior CausalSmith matching reductions use the full unfiltered perfect-matching orbit. Conditioning on a global spectral event produces correlated edge indicators and potentially an exponentially sparse support; matching-edge probabilities become ratios of stability-filtered counts. Consequently, neither the existing matching sampler nor its concentration argument targets the required distribution, and the diminishing-returns proof for the unfiltered prior need not survive conditioning.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A characterization of stability-conditioned edge marginals and a necessary-and-sufficient or verifiable sufficient condition for adaptive monotonicity and submodularity, or a minimal counterexample with a replacement policy bound, coupled to a conditioned sampler or ratio estimator with explicit bias and concentration guarantees.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly frames matching frequencies as actionable information for intervention choice; stability changes exactly the distribution underlying those frequencies.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Observational cyclic LiNG data leave a matching-indexed class -> interventions reveal the true matching -> greedy choices use matching-edge frequencies -> equilibrium semantics require frequencies conditional on the stable suborbit

method_exemplars.technique: Check adaptive monotonicity and diminishing conditional expected marginal gains over nested partial realizations before invoking adaptive-greedy guarantees.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A resolution must reproduce these inequalities under the conditioned realization law or identify the exact partial realizations where they fail.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate edge-outcome probabilities from sampled matchings and propagate concentration through the marginal-benefit functional.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the direct baseline estimator, but its sampling law and proof must be replaced by stability-conditioned analogues.

method_exemplars.technique: Use approximate generation, self-reducibility, annealing, and multiplicative error control for ratios of matching partition functions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Conditioned edge probabilities are ratios of filtered orbit counts, although the global spectral filter prevents direct reuse of the permanent chain.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize when Schur stability rho(B)<1 and absolute contractivity rho(|B|)<1 select the same normalized ICA row assignments, and determine the sharp orbit-count separation caused by signed feedback cancellation.

source_refs.claim: Cyclic LiNG stability is Schur stability of the signed coefficient matrix and can select among ICA-equivalent assignments.
source_refs.author: Gustavo Lacerda, Peter L. Spirtes, Joseph Ramsey, Patrik O. Hoyer

source_refs.claim: StableSpIn learns cyclic linear SCMs using a spectral-radius constraint on the entrywise absolute adjacency matrix.
source_refs.author: Panagiotis Misiakos, Markus Püschel

source_refs.claim: Cyclic SCMs require explicit solvability conditions because existence, uniqueness, and causal semantics can fail.
source_refs.author: Stephan Bongers, Patrick Forré, Jonas Peters, Joris M. Mooij

open_problems.why_unsolved: Absolute contractivity is a tractable sufficient condition but suppresses cancellation between positive and negative feedback paths and can therefore be strictly stronger than Schur stability. Row assignment and normalization change both signs and magnitudes, so agreement for one representative does not imply agreement throughout the orbit. The cited literatures use the predicates for different purposes without an SCC- and sign-pattern-level characterization of orbit-wise equivalence or the number of causally admissible alternatives discarded by the absolute criterion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient sign/SCC characterization for orbit-wise equivalence of rho(B)<1 and rho(|B|)<1, together with an explicit polynomial-bit rational family attaining a sharp separation between the two assignment counts.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its case for stability as a substantive and computational restriction, then isolate the difference between absolute-matrix regularization and equilibrium Schur stability.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Feedback models require stability -> absolute spectral-radius constraints enable scalable discovery -> signed cancellation can preserve Schur stability beyond absolute contractivity -> determine when the tractable restriction preserves the full ICA orbit

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce admissible row permutations to cycle reversals and track their signed cycle products and block-triangular spectra.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Cycle reversal exposes how normalization changes signed feedback and supplies the natural comparison unit for the two predicates.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Perron-Frobenius-compatible analysis of the entrywise absolute adjacency matrix and its spectral-radius constraint.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the destination predicate whose orbit-level equivalence to or separation from Schur stability must be established.

open_problems.open_problem: Derive the sharp equilibrium-effect identified set obtained by filtering the square cyclic LiNG row-assignment fiber to Schur-stable mechanisms.

source_refs.excerpt: The projection of this postintervention-solvable subset onto the effect equals the stated frontier.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The source-minimal frontier filters square admissible row permutations by postintervention solvability and then projects them onto response ratios. Schur stability is stricter and nonlocal, so it can eliminate effect witnesses without altering the deletion-rank certificate. The first proof step must replace the rank-only completion certificate by a simultaneous normalized-row, invertibility, and spectral-feasibility certificate, then prove that every retained effect value has an exact stable same-law witness.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit finite formula for the Schur-stable equilibrium-effect identified set, an exact stable witness for every value, and a necessary-and-sufficient condition under which stability collapses the unfiltered frontier to a singleton.

writing_exemplar.why: Its causal-effect identification framing keeps the destination centered on equilibrium responses rather than enumeration alone.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Non-Gaussian observations restrict compatible mechanisms -> compatible cyclic mechanisms can imply different causal effects -> equilibrium stability removes some mechanisms -> characterize the resulting sharp effect set

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate normalized admissible candidates, attach a spectral-feasibility certificate, and project each retained mechanism onto its equilibrium response.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is precisely the effect projection of a stability-filtered cyclic LiNG candidate class.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert a simultaneous confidence set over finitely many causal structures and project every retained structure onto the causal target.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a close confidence-set architecture for finite structural ambiguity and downstream causal projections.

literature_map:
Shimizu, Hoyer, Hyvärinen, and Kerminen (JMLR 2006; arXiv:1207.1413) establish ICA identification for acyclic LiNGAM up to scaling and permutation, with acyclicity selecting the row order.
Lacerda, Spirtes, Ramsey, and Hoyer (UAI 2008; arXiv:1206.3273) extend ICA to cyclic LiNG models, enumerate admissible assignments, and use Schur stability to narrow the class.
Hyvärinen and Smith (JMLR 2013) give likelihood-ratio estimators and a sufficient small-coefficient plus stability regime for unique cyclic identification, not an orbit-count classification.
Bongers, Forré, Peters, and Mooij (Annals of Statistics 2021; arXiv:1611.06221) explain why cyclic SCMs require explicit solvability and uniqueness conditions.
Ghassami et al. (ICML 2020, PMLR 119) characterize distribution and quasi-equivalence for cyclic linear Gaussian graphs, illustrating the richness of cyclic observational equivalence.
Dai, Ng, Zheng, Gao, and Zhang (AISTATS 2024; arXiv:2403.14843) recover local cyclic-LiNG alternatives and discuss constraints needed to select globally stable solutions locally.
Sharifian, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash (NeurIPS 2025; arXiv:2509.21423) represent the equivalence class by perfect matchings, prove SCC invariance, and base adaptive interventions on matching frequencies without conditioning on stability.
Misiakos and Püschel (UAI 2026, PMLR 337) impose rho(|B|)<1, creating a live distinction between absolute contractivity and signed Schur stability.
Valiant (SIAM Journal on Computing 1979; DOI:10.1137/0208032) supplies the #P framework and exact counting reductions.
Jerrum, Sinclair, and Vigoda (JACM 2004; DOI:10.1145/1008731.1008738) give an FPRAS for every nonnegative permanent and thus for the unfiltered matching orbit.
Dyer, Frieze, and Jerrum (SIAM Journal on Computing 2002) and Sly (FOCS 2010; arXiv:1005.5584) provide bounded-degree independent-set approximation-hardness donors.
Uno (ISAAC 1997; DOI:10.1007/3-540-63890-3_11) gives bounded-delay enumeration machinery for all bipartite perfect matchings.
Miettinen, Taskinen, Nordhausen, and Oja (Statistical Science 2015; arXiv:1406.4765) derive estimating equations and asymptotic laws for FOBI but do not propagate uncertainty through a discrete causal orbit.
Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (Econometrica 2007; DOI:10.1111/j.1468-0262.2007.00794.x) provide confidence-region inversion for set-valued parameters.
Pfanzagl (Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference 1998; DOI:10.1016/S0378-3758(98)00121-9) supplies local-uniform confidence obstructions for discontinuous functionals, supporting pointwise-only count inference near stability boundaries.
